title: Monthly Competitive Programming Contest — January 2025
excerpt: Competing as team SEU_HOTASHA in the SEUCC Monthly Competitive Programming Contest in January 2025, solving algorithmic challenges and celebrating problem-solving milestones.
author: Fazley Rabbi
cover_alt: A large group photograph of participants, organizers, and SEUCC members holding colorful balloons after the Monthly Competitive Programming Contest.
body:
## A Platform to Learn, Compete, and Improve

In **January 2025**, the **Southeast Computer Club (SEUCC)** hosted the **Monthly Competitive Programming Contest**. Competing alongside my teammates under team name **SEU_HOTASHA**, this contest was the perfect platform to learn, compete, and improve problem-solving skills under timed conditions.

## Engaging Contest Environment

The contest computer lab was filled with energy and enthusiasm. Participants tackled a series of algorithmic and logic problems. Colorful balloons floated across the room, celebrating each accepted solution and adding excitement to team SEU_HOTASHA's contest experience.

## Collaboration and Community Growth

Competing together and discussing problem approaches after the contest fostered a great sense of community among fellow programmers. Events like this monthly contest organized by SEUCC continue to motivate students across Southeast University to sharpen their coding skills, embrace competitive programming, and prepare for national and international contests.

These photographs capture the full group celebration with SEUCC, the contest lab in action, and memorable moments with team SEU_HOTASHA holding solved-problem balloons.


## Key Takeaways (কী শিখলাম)

- **Setting Benchmark Standards:** Starting the year with an intense team contest established high accountability and clear algorithmic goals for the competitive season.
- **Effective Division of Labor:** Practiced delegating problem sets based on individual member strengths across graph theory, string processing, and combinatorics.
- **Post-Contest Upsolving:** Reaffirmed the golden rule that the greatest learning happens after the contest by thoroughly analyzing and upsolving all unsolved problems.
